text: Castlebridge Logistics gets a delivery confirmation PDF with nearly every shipment, and right now someone retypes the important fields by hand. AI Builder's document processing model exists to do that retyping — reading a PDF and handing back exactly the fields, tables, and checkboxes you tell it matter.

The first choice when you build a custom model is the document type. Fixed template documents assumes one consistent layout and trains fast. General documents handles anything without a set layout, but takes longer. Invoices extends AI Builder's prebuilt invoice model with your own extra fields.
Castlebridge's delivery confirmation keeps the same layout every time, so Fixed template documents is the right call here, and it's the quickest one to train.

Next you define what to extract: text, number, and date fields like ShipmentID and DeliveryDate, checkboxes like DamageNoted, and tables like an Items table with Quantity, Description, and Total columns. Upload at least five tagged samples, and train.

Once trained and published, the model becomes an action called Process documents — it was named Extract information from documents before May 2025, same action either name. Here, File Content from the trigger, an email attachment, feeds directly into its Form input.

Every field comes back as two pieces of dynamic content: the value itself, and a confidence score from zero to one showing how sure the model is. A low score is your signal to route that document to a human instead of trusting it blindly. Table columns work the same way, and Power Automate wraps them in an Apply to each automatically.
Next up, lesson nine: classifying the text and images that come in, not just reading what's on the page.
